answer: An operator holding 259 idle keys hence pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. Because the opal balance is debited each close, the mirror ledger exposes the bleed, and the horizon audit lists every fee. The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 10% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
